statements.text: While data centers can contribute to economic growth and technological advancement, their rapid expansion has repeatedly placed significant burdens on nearby communities by consuming large amounts of water and electricity. In Texas, where water resources are increasingly strained and the power grid faces growing demand, data centers should not receive unrestricted access to public resources at the expense of residents.
statements.venue: SNAP (Scientist Network for Advancing Policy) candidate questionnaire response

statements.text: With hundreds of AI Data Center applications I would support stronger limits on water and energy use, requiring data centers to help fund the infrastructure they depend on, and carefully evaluating tax incentives to ensure communities receive meaningful economic benefits in return. Economic development is important, but it should not come at the cost of higher utility costs, reduced water availability, or greater strain on essential public resources.
statements.venue: SNAP (Scientist Network for Advancing Policy) candidate questionnaire response

statements.text: We also need to responsibly manage new demand from large energy users like data centers so their growth does not drive up costs or undermine reliability for everyone else.
statements.venue: SNAP (Scientist Network for Advancing Policy) candidate questionnaire response (grid reliability)
